You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Construct the described 30x30 input exactly, then add sequence-ordered connectors.
N=30
g=[[1]*N for _ in range(N)]
# Three-by-three framed cells: each cell is 6x6 with 8 interior background.
row_starts=[1,9,16]
col_starts=[1,10,20]
vals=[[2,4,3],[3,6,9],[9,4,5]]
for br, rs in enumerate(row_starts):
    for bc, cs in enumerate(col_starts):
        for r in range(rs,rs+6):
            for c in range(cs,cs+6): g[r][c]=8
        for r in range(rs+2,rs+4):
            for c in range(cs+2,cs+4): g[r][c]=vals[br][bc]
# Bottom sequence row
seq=[2,4,3,9,5,4,6,3,9]
for i,v in enumerate(seq): g[28][1+2*i]=v
# Color the separators along the path of marker positions in sequence.
# Horizontal steps: rows are the marker's two rows, fill columns between cell frames.
# 1->2: top-left to top-middle; 2->3: top-middle to top-right
for r in [3,4]:
    for c in range(7,10): g[r][c]=2
    for c in range(16,20): g[r][c]=4
# 3->4 and 4->5 vertical steps; right column down twice
for r in [7,8]:
    for c in [22,23]: g[r][c]=3
for c in [22,23]: g[15][c]=9
# bottom-right to bottom-middle, horizontal left
for r in [18,19]:
    for c in range(16,20): g[r][c]=5
# bottom-middle to center: upward, color 4 in row 15
for c in [12,13]: g[15][c]=4
# center to middle-left, horizontal left
for r in [11,12]:
    for c in range(7,10): g[r][c]=6
# middle-left to bottom-left, vertical down
for c in [3,4]: g[15][c]=3
assert len(g)==30 and all(len(row)==30 for row in g)
# Show only modified rows and ensure modeled structure sizes
[(i, ' '.join(map(str,g[i]))) for i in [3,4,7,8,11,12,15,18,19,28]]
